Anonymous

/uh-NAH-nuh-mus/ — stress on NAH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something or someone anonymous has an identity that is unknown or kept secret.

An anonymous donor paid off the entire school lunch debt.

Worked Example

An anonymous benefactor left a quarter million dollars to the children's hospital, but staff could not learn the donor's identity.

An- (without) + onym (name, from the Greek root in synonym and antonym) + -ous (full of, possessing the quality) = without a name, or full of being nameless. This is a stacked-prefix word—two reusable morphemes in one. Knowing onym unlocks synonym (same name), antonym (opposite name), and pseudonym (false name).

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unnamed: having no name given or stated

unidentified: not yet recognized or known

incognito: hiding one's identity on purpose

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

onymous: bearing a name (rare, technical term)

identified: having a known, openly stated identity

Where it sits · how deliberately who they are stays hidden — unfamiliar → unnamed → unidentified → anonymous

unfamiliar vs. anonymous: An unfamiliar face is simply new to you, but an anonymous one belongs to someone whose identity stays deliberately hidden.

unnamed vs. anonymous: An unnamed source just wasn't mentioned by name; an anonymous source insists that no one ever learn who they are.

unidentified vs. anonymous: An unidentified caller hasn't been recognized yet, but an anonymous caller made sure they never will be.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-

Prefix — an-: without (Greek)

Root — onym

Root — onym: name (the same root as in synonym, antonym, pseudonym) (Greek (onyma))

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of (Latin (-osus))

Put it together

Put it together: This is the unit's one special triple-decomposition word — three parts instead of the usual two: the prefix an- ('without') + the Greek root onym ('name,' the same root as in synonym and pseudonym) + the suffix -ous ('full of'). Put together, anonymous means 'full of without-a-name-ness' — having an identity that is unknown or kept secret.

Use the root in a new word: pseudonym

Use the root in a new word: pseudonym: The novelist published her mysteries under a pseudonym to keep her real identity secret.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for anonymous when identity is hidden, unknown, or deliberately withheld. It works for people ('an anonymous caller'), products ('anonymous web browsing'), and attributions ('anonymous donations'). The word emphasizes the absence of a known name, not the reason for the concealment.
